title: Article 14 - Equality before law
content: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. Manifest arbitrariness is antithetical to equality (E.P. Royappa doctrine). Foundational for gender equality and non-discrimination in personal laws.
high_yield_takeaway: Cornerstone of Fundamental Rights and Rule of Law; used to strike down arbitrary executive actions and ensure gender justice.

title: Article 19 - Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
content: All citizens shall have the right to freedom of speech and expression, peaceful assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession. Subject to reasonable restrictions under Art 19(2) on sovereignty, public order, and morality.
high_yield_takeaway: Vital for media freedom, hate speech laws, internet bans (Anuradha Bhasin), and peaceful assembly.

title: Article 21 - Protection of life and personal liberty
content: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Substantively expanded via Maneka Gandhi (1978) to require just, fair, and reasonable procedure, and Puttaswamy (2017) to include privacy.
high_yield_takeaway: The expansive ark of the Constitution encompassing privacy, dignity, health, livelihood, and speedy trial.

title: Article 25 - Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
content: Subject to public order, morality and health and to the other provisions of this Part, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion. State can regulate secular activities associated with religious practice and provide for social welfare.
high_yield_takeaway: Essential religious practices test; key tension with Uniform Civil Code (Art 44) and gender equality in personal laws.

title: Article 32 - Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part
keywords: Heart and soul of the Constitution
content: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights is guaranteed. The Supreme Court shall have power to issue directions, orders or writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari). Termed the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
high_yield_takeaway: Primary tool for judicial review and human rights protection. Basic structure of the Constitution.

title: Article 44 - Uniform Civil Code for the citizens
content: The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India. Non-justiciable DPSP intended to foster secular integration and gender parity across succession, marriage, and adoption.
high_yield_takeaway: Frequently debated regarding secularism vs religious freedom (Art 25), gender rights (Shah Bano, Sarla Mudgal).

title: Article 74 - Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
content: There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice. Provided the President may require the Council to reconsider advice once.
high_yield_takeaway: Establishes parliamentary executive supremacy; President bound by cabinet advice (Shamsher Singh doctrine).

title: Article 123 - Power of President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament
content: If at any time Parliament is not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action, he may promulgate an Ordinance. Must be laid before Parliament within 6 weeks of reassembly.
high_yield_takeaway: Subject to judicial review for colorable exercise of power and fraud on the Constitution (D.C. Wadhwa & Krishna Kumar Singh rulings).

title: Article 142 - Enforcement of decrees and orders of Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc.
content: The Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
high_yield_takeaway: Used by the Apex Court in Bhopal Gas tragedy, Ayodhya title suit, releasing long-term prisoners (Perarivalan), and framing interim guidelines (Vishaka).

title: Article 163 - Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor
content: There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor, except in so far as he is by or under this Constitution required to act in his discretion. If any question arises whether a matter falls under Governor's discretion, the Governor's decision shall be final.
high_yield_takeaway: Broader discretionary latitude than the President; core flashpoint in Centre-State conflicts and federal balance (Nabam Rebia 2016 curtailed arbitrary usage).

title: Article 174 - Sessions of the State Legislature, prorogation and dissolution
content: The Governor shall from time to time summon the House or each House of the Legislature of the State to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, but six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.
high_yield_takeaway: Governor can summon the house only on aid and advise of Cabinet, except when the government has prima facie lost majority (Nabam Rebia / Shiv Sena rulings).

title: Article 200 - Assent to Bills passed by State Legislature
content: When a Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly, it shall be presented to the Governor and the Governor shall declare either that he assents to the Bill, or that he withholds assent therefrom, or that he reserves the Bill for the consideration of the President, or returns it with a message 'as soon as possible'.
high_yield_takeaway: SC (2023 Punjab & Telangana Governor rulings) held that Governor cannot sit indefinitely on bills or kill them through pocket veto; key safeguard for federal balance.

title: Article 239AA - Special provisions with respect to Delhi
content: As from the commencement of the Constitution (69th Amendment) Act, 1991, the Union Territory of Delhi shall be called the National Capital Territory of Delhi, with an elected Legislative Assembly empowered to make laws on State and Concurrent List items except Public Order, Police, and Land.
high_yield_takeaway: Apex Court (2018 & 2023 Constitution Benches) affirmed elected government's executive control over civil services and representative democracy.

title: Article 262 - Adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers
content: Parliament may by law provide for the adjudication of any dispute or complaint with respect to the use, distribution or control of the waters of, or in, any inter-State river or river valley. Parliament may by law exclude jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
high_yield_takeaway: Crucial federal dispute mechanism; criticized for prolonged tribunal delays and enforcement deadlocks.

title: Article 263 - Provisions with respect to an Inter-State Council
content: If at any time it appears to the President that the public interests would be served by the establishment of a Council charged with investigating and discussing subjects in which some or all of the States, or the Union and one or more of the States, have a common interest.
high_yield_takeaway: Permanent constitutional institutional forum for cooperative federalism; recommended by Sarkaria & Punchhi Commissions to meet at least 3 times a year.

title: Article 279A - Goods and Services Tax Council
content: The President shall constitute a Council to be called the Goods and Services Tax Council. The Council consists of the Union Finance Minister (Chairperson), Union Minister of State, and State Finance Ministers. Decisions taken by 3/4th weighted majority (Union 1/3rd, States 2/3rd).
high_yield_takeaway: Pinnacle of collaborative fiscal federalism; SC (Mohit Minerals 2022) held recommendations have persuasive value, upholding cooperative federalism.

title: Article 280 - Finance Commission
content: The President shall constitute a Finance Commission consisting of a Chairman and four other members every fifth year or earlier to make recommendations regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between Union and States, and allocation between the States.
high_yield_takeaway: The constitutional balancing wheel of fiscal federalism addressing vertical and horizontal fiscal imbalances.

title: Article 324 - Superintendence, direction and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission
content: The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to Parliament and to the Legislature of every State shall be vested in the Election Commission.
high_yield_takeaway: Plenary power to ensure free and fair elections. SC (Anoop Baranwal 2023) established independent selection panel for Election Commissioners.

title: Article 356 - Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States
content: If the President, on receipt of report from the Governor of a State or otherwise, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution, the President may by Proclamation assume to himself all or any functions of State government.
high_yield_takeaway: Dr. Ambedkar hoped it would remain a 'dead letter'; heavily abused historically; disciplined by S.R. Bommai (1994) establishing judicial review, mandatory floor tests, and safeguarding federal balance.

title: Article 368 - Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor
content: Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article.
high_yield_takeaway: Subordinate to the Basic Structure Doctrine; Parliament cannot alter the essential identity and core values of the Constitution (Kesavananda Bharati).

title: Tenth Schedule - Anti-Defection Law
content: Introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985. Sets provisions for disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defection (voluntarily giving up membership or voting contrary to party whip). Decided by Speaker/Chairman.
high_yield_takeaway: Criticized for stifling intra-party dissent and Speaker's partisan delays; Kihoto Hollohan (1992) established judicial review over Speaker's final order.
